tests.title: integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 1. creates a customer with a mailing address and a job for it
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 2. logs two time entries, one charge and one non-billable entry (total = quantity × unit_cost)
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 3. Create Invoice eligibility lists the customer with the billable total and the engine total
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 4. month 1 finalize creates one parent invoice, stamps the transactions and stores the PDF zip in S3
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 4b. time-travel: re-dates the month-1 statement 31 days back so the next finalize is a real month 2
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 5. partial payment inserts a child snapshot and preserves the issued parent
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 6. write-off of part of the remainder inserts a snapshot and preserves the issued parent
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 7. billing engine, Account Audit and Accounts Receivable agree on the month-1 remaining
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 8a. month 2 finalize rolls the remaining forward as beginning_balance and zeroes the absorbed month-1 rows
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 8b. the three views agree on the month-2 remaining and the audit reports no stale rolled-forward rows
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 8d. the closing snapshot carries the statement date as YYYY-MM-DD
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 8c. right after the month-2 finalize the engine has nothing new to bill (no re-credited write-off)
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 9. a payment referencing the ABSORBED month-1 statement is remapped to the current chain and annotated
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 10. an overpayment with captureOverpayment settles the chain and banks the excess as a Prepayment retainer
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 11. reversing the overpayment (NSF) restores the chain remaining with a positive payment row
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 12a. deleting the reversal (latest snapshot) restores the chain exactly to its post-overpayment state
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 12b. deleting the reversal restores the original payment note (it must be reversible again)
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 12c. deleting a non-retainer payment leaves unrelated retainers untouched
integration: month-end ledger lifecycle (HTTP) 13. finalizing the same customer twice on the same day does not create a second parent or double the outstanding
